_comment: Rewrites French lessons 10-17 into the six-archetype variety plan in scripts/content/lessons/FRENCH-VARIETY.md. Each lesson keeps every exercise it already had, in the archetype's slot order with the -meet choice first and the listening model last, and gains exactly one new `transform` exercise built only from material the lesson (or its prerequisites) already teaches. Existing exercises are byte-identical to the manifest. Applied by scripts/content/differentiate-first-words.py; do not edit courses/ by hand.

exercises.prompt: Which French word means “yes/no question opening”?
exercises.explanation: Est-ce que introduces a yes/no question without changing subject-verb order: Est-ce que tu travailles ? You can also ask Tu travailles ? with rising intonation. Qui asks who. This lesson uses the est-ce que frame.

exercises.prompt: Which French word means “my (masculine singular)”?
exercises.explanation: Mon and ma mean my; they agree with the thing owned, not the owner. Use mon livre and ma maison. French does not put le or la before these possessives. Mes is plural for either gender.

exercises.prompt: The book belongs to the person you are speaking to now. Say it with ton: Mon livre est blanc.
exercises.explanation: Ton is the masculine singular possessive for your, so it takes the place of mon and nothing else changes: Ton livre est blanc. It agrees with livre, the thing owned, not with the owner.

exercises.prompt: Which French word means “tomorrow”?
exercises.explanation: French often expresses a plan with aller + infinitive: je vais étudier means I am going to study. Keep vais conjugated, and leave étudier in the infinitive. Demain means tomorrow. This differs from je vais à Paris, which names a destination.
